contexts.text: He who does not apperceive [that] what is good and true is from the Lord, is no longer in Heaven.
In the other life, where perception far surpasses such apperception.
Hence the mental view, apperception, and utterance of singular things is more prompt (after death).
I apperceived... that he was lifted up.
As soon as evil Spirits... apperceive as it were by smell anything which is delightful to a man...
Those who feel hatred apperceive a kind of delight... in it.
I apperceived that I had been in a state like...
When anything contrary to the truth of conscience inflows... they not only apperceive it, but...
The pains... take away the apperception of the... freedom.
Unless he can apperceive and feel this, he has not anything rational...
The interior hearing apprehends; the interior sight then perceives; and thence through the hearing there is an apperception of the meaning...
Cannot inflow perceptibly into man's idea.
Conscience is a species of perception; for to act against or according to conscience, is nothing else than to apperceive thence...
To see = to understand and apperceive... AC 3132. AC 5274. AC 5639. AC 6675. AC 8460.
Human rational truth... apperceived that it was not what it ought to be. Signified.
I have often apperceived their resistance.
They could apperceive the interiors of my thoughts.

Influx of the light of Heaven into the things of the light of the world produces illustration, and at the same time apperception. If there iis correspondence, [it produces] an apperception of what is true; if not, an apperception of what is false as if it were true. But there can be no illustration and apperception without affection. AC 3336:2.
Unless the light of Heaven inflowed, no one would have any apperception...
The light of truth from the Lord cannot (then) inflow, and give them to apperceive that it is so...
The simple who are in good... can apperceive in a moment... They have a general sense of the apperception of truth.
In seeing to see = to apperceive, and thus to know for certain.
All apperception in the natural world is from the Rational.
The apperception of natural truth. Signified.
To say = to perceive; here, to apperceive, because from the Natural AC 3609.
The Rational... is above the sphere of the apperception (of the Natural).
A state of the apperception of the affection of truth from influx through Divine truth. Signified, Explained.
He would then apperceive in what way falsities had intermingled themselves.
This cause in no wise appears to man, because it is above the sphere of his apperception.
Light as of dawn then appears to him, if he is in such a state that he can apperceive it.
Conscience... is the interior apperception of good and truth...

The communication of the thought and apperception of the spirit with the speech and hearing of the body... The apperception of speech is nothing but the hearing of the spirit... When a man is listening, the apperception appears no otherwise than as the hearing in the ear.
From good they apperceive truth.
To tell = apperception; thus communication. AC 5264. AC 5601, Explained.

To hear = to obey, and also to apperceive. That it also = to apperceive, is evident from the very function of the ear... (which is) to receive what another says, and carry it away to the general sensory, in order that this may apperceive what the other is thinking... In the languages... to hear anyone is to apperceive; and to listen to anyone is to obey... Hence it is that the Spirits and Angels who correspond to the ear... are not only apperceptions, but also obediences... Being obediences, they are also apperceptions, for the one involves the other.
Through this influx (of interior things into exterior ones) comes apperception... The interior man sees and apperceives in the exterior what is going on outside the latter.
That which reigns universally is not apperceived, except when the thought is determined thereto.

That it would turn out well, is an apperception from the Sensuous, which apperception is relatively obscure. There actually are an apperception from the Sensuous, an apperception from the interior Natural, and an apperception from the Rational. For when man is in interior thought from affection, and abstracts the mind from sensuous things... he is in rational apperception... But when man is in exterior thought... his apperception is from the interior Natural... But when man is in pleasures, and in the delights of the love of the world, and also of the love of self, the apperception is from the Sensuous... The more exterior the apperception is, the more obscure it is...
The holiness in each particular of the Word does not appear to the understanding... but still, through influx from Heaven, it does to the apperception with him who believes the Word to be holy.

Thou hearest a dream to interpret it = the faculty of apperceiving what there is in the things foreseen. To hear of thee = to apperceive and know that he has such a faculty... To hear = to apperceive.
The apperception of the Natural. Signified.
That nothing shall be apperceived (in the Natural) of the truth there was before. Signified.
The apperception of truth is from good; for the Lord is in good, and gives the apperception.
Apperception in both Naturals, in general and in particular. Signified.
What apperception from the truths and the good of truth in the Natural is, can indeed be explained; but does not fall into the understanding...
These are the things he wanted to apperceive.
An apperception from the Celestial of the Spiritual of the spiritual medium present with the truths. Signified, Explained.
An apperception that good would be adjoined to truths. Signified.
It appears that sensation, and also apperception, come by influx from the external, but... the internal inflows into the external... to the end that it may thence apperceive and be perfected.
Apperception from spiritual good. Signified.
I said... = apperception that... To say = perception.
An apperception that he will perish. Signified.

The Lord does not openly teach truths... but through good leads to think what is true; and also inspires, unknown to the man, the apperception and thence the choice that this is true, because the Word says so...
To say = perception; thus also apperception.
These filthy things are apperceived by the Angels milder than they really are... The angelic apperception [of them] has been given me, which was such that I was not at all horrified. Explained.
Thus man is in the midst, and does not apperceive either evil or good.

The Word ought to be searched... When this is done from the affection of truth, the man is illustrated by the Lord, so as to apperceive, without knowing whence, what is true. (Compare with AC 5937:3, and AC 7055:2.)
As Spirits possess all things of the thought and will, and Angels the things still more interior... the man cannot but apperceive and feel that it is he himself who thinks and wills.
Hence is man's apperception of a Thing. Explained.
An eminent apperception. Signified.

This Intellectual of the Church is more interior than the Intellectual which is only from scientifics; for it is an apperception that it is so, not because scientific and philosophical things declare it; but because the Word in its spiritual sense does.
Apperception by the truth of the Natural. Signified.
Apperception concerning the Intellectual and the Voluntary of the Church. Signified.
His obscure apperception. Signified, Explained.
While the spiritual are being introduced, they do not perceive good, because it inflows into the affection of truth from within; thus they are not in apperception before they have been regenerated.
Influx into the power of his obscure apperception. Signified... The reason the apperception is said to be obscure, is that the spiritual, relatively to the Celestial, are in obscurity.
Apperception of truth and good inflowing... Signified.
Apperception concerning these scientific truths in the Natural. Signified.

The reason the Natural is in obscurity, is that it is in the light of the world, and at the same time in worldly things; and, when the light of Heaven inflows into these things, the apperception becomes obscure.
She saw him that he was good = the apperception that it [came] through Heaven.
The apperception of truth, that it was vile among false scientific. Signified.
The apperception that truths were being infested by falsities. Signified.
They were (then) mute, because they acknowledged that such was the case from the apperception then given them.
That the Law Divine will give to those of the Lord's Spiritual Kingdom to apperceive. Signified. To say = to apperceive; here, to give to apperceive.
The apperception then that the Lord is the only God. Signified. To Know = to apperceive.
Explorations (after death) take place in order that they themselves may apperceive that they cannot but be condemned.
Power from order that they became dull as to the apperception of truth. Signified, Explained... Fallacies cause truths not to be apperceived...
Influx and thence reception, and thus apperception. Signified.
Into the apperception of all those who were infesting. Signified. The eyes = apperception.
The apperception that the Lord alone is the God of the Church. Signified.
To say = to apperceive. References.
From the presence of Truth Divine there is apperception. Signified.
To look back = the deprivation of apperception; for man is deprived of apperception when he looks back or turns away from the truth which is from the Divine.
The apperception of that truth by those who inflict damnation. Signified, Explained.
The presence of the Lord in truth accommodated to apperception. Signified, Explained.
So long as (these) delights dominate, interior good cannot come to the apperception.
The immediate influx of truth from the Lord, from which [comes] not the apperception of truth; but the light which gives the faculty of understanding.
Apperceive that externals are to be taken away from them...
If truth Divine appeared as it is in Heaven... at the first view, and at the first apperception, man would reject it...
Mental view takes place by means of spiritual truth, and is apperception.

So long as the fires of evil are kept shut up in the will, the understanding is in light, and thence in the apperception of good and truth. But when those fires shed their light into the understanding, then the former light is dissipated, and the man is darkened in respect to the apperception of good and truth.

The truths of faith come to man's apperception, but not the good of charity, before he has been regenerated. For... the good of charity inflows through an internal way... and therefore does not come to the apperception.
This has been confirmed by many things which have come to [my] apperception.
Scientific truths are in man's memory. When they are taken out thence they come to the apperception.
The Word in the letter is no otherwise attended to and apperceived in Heaven...
He is then led by the Lord to apperceive and imbue the truths which are suited to him...
When man lives according to the Word, the Lord insinuates good into his life; hence the man apperceives it, and feels it... Otherwise it does not appear, because it is not apperceived.
It is known that the things seen with the eyes and heard with the ears are apperceived within the man...
The Israelitish nation, when it did not apperceive in the Word anything from Heaven. Signified, Explained. To see, when predicated of the understanding of the Word, = apperception. References.
Representative insignia of obedience, and of the apperception of the delights of external loves. Signified, Explained... The ears = obedience and apperception. References.
The apperception of the quality of the interiors of that nation. Signified. To hear = survey and apperception.
The apperception of internal Divine truth in external. Signified.
This interior resistance does not then come to man's apperception. Explained.
The apperception of those who are in the externals of the Church, etc., without the internals. Signified.
The natural man does not apperceive that thought.
They suppose (this), because it is so apperceived.
Hence it was apperceived what Angels they were...
He afterwards apperceives and acknowledges that he is a Spirit...
I say this from the apperception of it.
I have apperceived its increase and decrease...
He apperceived in his own way...
When they apperceive (this) they are ashamed.
It was apperceived that their influx is tender...
I have often apperceived (this).

The things which man thinks spiritually, he does not apperceive... But when he comes into the Spiritual World, he does not apperceive the things he had thought naturally, but those he had thought spiritually.
This it was given to apperceive by communication.
Man can think from the understanding, and thence apperceive what is true and also what is good, but cannot think it from the will, unless he wills and does it.
Apperception, which is internal hearing, is possible only in a substance which is an organic form.
I apperceived that I had been in such a state...
The Spirit apperceives no otherwise... But it is an appearance.
The light of Heaven... gives to the sight of the Angels to apperceive and distinguish the most minute things.

The hearing corresponds to their perception, which is of both the understanding and the will, and therefore in the tone and words of a speaker they apperceive the most minute things of his affection and thought...
To proceed is to be... presented in a suitable form so that it is apperceived and appears.
In order that (these things) may be presented to the apperception before the senses...
Thinks of others according to what he has heard and apperceived...
They apperceived in themselves infernal torment instead of heavenly joy.
The Angels do not apperceive anything about these men when the Word is being read by man... but instead of them they perceive the Lord.
When the Angels apperceive this, they leave him.
When (the Papists) apperceive in the other life that the Lord has all Power...
This fire burns inwardly, as is apperceived from the heat exhaled thence.
(This) it has been given me to know by many experiences, and also to apperceive.
Wherever they apperceive good affections, they turn them into evil ones...
Thought in the spirit... is not manifestly apperceived.
As (when a man is dying) they apperceive nothing but wind, they judge... that the spirit is not a man.
The very affection of truth is apperceived no otherwise than...
There are infinite things in the heat and light which proceed from the Lord, although they are apperceived simply as heat and light.
Hence from the light is thought, apperception, reflection, etc.
Charles XII excelled in the faculty of apperceiving; for, when in interior thought, he could run through a hundred things with one glance of the eye... SE 4752.
That the infernals have the gift of apperception. Explained.
It has been given me to apperceive continually that each and all things inflow...
When what is believed is seen and perceived, it is not then called faith; but apperception and perception.
The rivers of Egypt = Knowledges, and apperceptions of truth; because... the natural man has Knowledge and apperception; as the spiritual man has intelligence.
